newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker on strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker on strong U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, following U.S. fixed-income markets lower on the release of stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data, analysts said.

"It's all the U.S. really. Canada is looking toward tomorrow's data before establishing a clear bias, so in the interim we're just following U.S. treasuries lower," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with Technical Data.
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 fell C$0.50 to C$101.60 to yield 7.854 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 21/32 to yield 7.04 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 81 basis points from 83 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian and U.S. debt markets weakened after the Commerce Department reported that second quarter U.S. gross domestic product was revised up to show a 4.8 percent annualized pace of growth. Economists had expected a 4.2 percent figure.

Another U.S. economic report released later in the session weakened markets further. The second report showed a surprising 7.9 percent annualized increase in sales of new single-family homes for July.
"Both reports showed strength in the economy, a lot more than was anticipated," said Philip Strathy, vice-president of Strathy Investments Ltd.

Canadian investors were awaiting release of Canada's real GDP and the current account balance for the second quarter. The current account report is expected to show a surplus for the first time in more than a decade.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it will auction C$3.0 billion in 6.25 percent bonds due September, 1998 on September 4.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.30 to C$97.20 to yield 7.393 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 15/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 54 basis points from 57 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 4.03 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.23 percent.
